Every node has exactly d neighbors, so the graphs have 8, 12, and 16 edges; which pairs get joined is random, and the d=2 graph here splits into a triangle and a five-cycle rather than one long cycle." width="100%"} Creates `n` nodes and joins them so that each one has exactly `d` neighbors, with no self-loops or parallel edges, giving `n * d / 2` edges in all. The graph is built by pairing stubs: every node gets `d` stubs, the stubs are shuffled and paired off, and pairs that would make a self-loop or repeat an edge are set aside and paired again. If the leftover stubs can't be joined, the construction starts over. For `d` small compared with `n` the result is close to uniform over all `d`-regular graphs. The process follows NetworkX's `random_regular_graph()`, whose arguments come in the order `(d, n)`. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Random regular graphs are useful for: - null models in which every node has the same degree, so any structure comes from the wiring alone - expanders: for `d >= 3` they are connected and well-mixing with high probability - testing algorithms whose behavior depends on degree heterogeneity ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. `n * d` must be even. [d]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Degree of every node. Must be less than `n` (unless both are `0`). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` or `d=` is negative, `n * d` is odd, or `d=` is not less than `n=`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Twenty nodes of degree three have `20 * 3 / 2 = 30` edges: ::: {#5e0bd3cf .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_random_regular_graph(n=20, d=3, seed=5) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (20, 30) ``` ::: ::: Every node has the same degree: ::: {#08f85db5 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} set(graph.degrees(return_dict=True).values()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {3} ``` ::: ::: With `d=3` the graph is almost always connected, and its diameter stays small: ::: {#0260722b .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.is_connected(), graph.diameter() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (True, 6) ``` ::: :::
